generated_by: prism-parity:tools/generate-vector-storage.php for php; the ports' own runners for ts and py. Every packed string is execution output — a hand-authored base64 double would assert the author's model of IEEE 754.

cases.title: exact binary fractions
cases.notes: Every component is exactly representable, so any disagreement here is in the byte order or the width, not in float rounding. The control: if this row differs the format is wrong, and every other row is noise.

cases.title: a single component
cases.notes: One double. Pins that the format carries no length prefix, no padding and no header — a reader that expected any of those would fail here first.

cases.title: values with no exact binary form
cases.notes: The classic. 0.1 has no exact double, so this row pins that all three languages store the SAME inexact value rather than each rounding its own way. A language that parsed the literal differently would diverge here and nowhere else.

cases.title: full double precision
cases.notes: Seventeen significant digits. A format that round-tripped through a decimal string would lose the last one; this pins that it does not.

cases.title: alternating sign
cases.notes: Pins the sign bit across an even number of components, where a byte-order error inside a pair can cancel out and hide.

cases.title: both ends of the exponent range
cases.notes: Near the limits of a double. A format that narrowed to float32 anywhere in the path would overflow the second component to infinity and underflow the first to zero, and both would still base64 cleanly.

cases.title: eight components
cases.notes: Long enough that a chunking bug in the encoder has somewhere to show. Base64 encodes three bytes to four characters, so 64 bytes is not a multiple of the group size and the padding is exercised.

cases.title: no components at all
cases.notes: REFUSED in all three. An empty vector has no direction; storing one would put a row in the index that can never be scored and never be found.

cases.title: zero magnitude
cases.notes: REFUSED in all three, and the interesting one: it is not empty and every component is finite and valid. Its magnitude is zero, so similarity against it is undefined — and returning 0.0 would be a plausible-looking number rather than an answer.

divergence_note: Every row agrees. It did NOT when this suite was written: both ports asserted scorability lazily, at the first comparison, where the reference asserts it on the write path. vec-0006 and vec-0009 were stored by the ports and refused by the reference. That is not cosmetic -- a degenerate vector the ports accepted was written to a shared store, and every recall that later touched that row threw instead of returning results. Fixed in both ports rather than recorded as a divergence, because unlike G-20 and G-21 this one had a right answer.
